notes.text:
Trader Joe’s uses Service Channel and the Service Channel mobile app.
Customer Rules Must be followed! Note: Service Channel recognizes the phone GPS so tech needs to be within 2 miles of the store to log in/out.
 ***IMPORTANT*** If you are unable to log in or out of Service Channel – you can use our phone based automated response system (IVR) by dialing 516-500-7776. Take pictures of login error and save to dispatch
Techs need to check into Service Channel work order when arriving on location.
1.	After checking into Service Channel, techs should head in store and ask to speak with Captain/Manager on Duty. Introduce yourself and explain why you are onsite.
2.	Once you are shown equipment needing diagnosing, take pictures of data tags and asset tags. Specifically, pictures of Model and Serial number are mandatory.
3.	Once diagnosis is complete, confirm NTE on work order and determine if fixes can be completed same day.  
4.	If yes, assuming under NTE, tech can source parts locally to complete same day repairs but MUST call Climate Pros purchasing team for Tech PO (630-283-7316).
5.	If yes, but NTE will be exceeded, techs need to call their SM or CSS Keri Adams at 224-315-7139.
6.	If no verbal approval is given, techs need to move dispatch to PUR: NEED PARTS and check out of store with MOD.
7.	All return work MUST be quoted and submitted to the FM for approval unless verbal approval has been obtained.
8.	Once back in vehicle, techs should update FJX dispatch notes AND Service Channel work order notes. 
9.	Move Service Channel work order to correct status:
10.	In Progress/Incomplete or In Progress/Awaiting Quote if we cannot repair same day. 
11.	COMPLETED/PENDING CONFIRMATION if work is complete.

***Refrigerant adds - All refrigerant adds MUST be logged in SC and in dispatch notes. NO EXCEPTIONS. Dispatch notes, parts tab, and refrigerant tracking form should match the amount of the gas add.  Once refrigerant added, Service Channel work order should be moved to COMPLETED/PENDING REFRIGERANT USE so Customer Success Teams can track usage. Techs need to be mindful of question about refrigerant use in Service Channel. If refrigerant is used, they must answer YES.**

***Trader Joe’s EMS/Monitoring is R3 Contacts
Rick Furgison 971-235-4175
Cristian Alexander 509-496-9772
Travis Rider 702-592-5151

***ACORN RELATED ISSUES - If you are on a Trader Joe's Call and find that the issue is related to Acorn, please call 24hr #860-863-5924 for Power & Process***  

For any other questions about Trader Joe’s, please email Traderjoes@climatepros.com or call Keri Adams (Customer Success Supervisor) at (224) 315-7139

I had to fill the trash can with water about 7 times to fully de-ice the case. I was watching the temp drop, but due to the store closing, I didn't see it hit setpoint, but it was cooling and everything was working.

As of July 10, 2023, technicians no longer have to call (or text) the H-E-B refrigerant hotline to get approval to add refrigerant. 

Instead, technicians and/or vendor recordkeepers MUST create a “call log” in MyFacility within 72 hours of the refrigerant add, documenting: 
•	The appliance serviced.
•	The refrigerant type added.
•	Total amount of refrigerant recovered (if any)
•	Total amount of refrigerant added (including adding back recovered refrigerant)
•	Date refrigerant was added. 
•	Leak location(s) 

There will be an additional optional free text space for other notes.  

**PLEASE copy and paste the following link to access the HEB COMPRESSOR REPLACEMENT FORM:

https://url.us.m.mimecastprotect.com/s/OVkRCQWRVRFxmxD1SxfnTGgCW1?domain=app.smartsheet.com

Technicians and/or vendor record keepers MUST record refrigerant adds on the following appliance types:
•	Any refrigeration appliance except for self-contains (e.g., bottle coolers on the store floor), regardless of charge size.
•	Any HVAC appliance, regardless of charge size
A note on HVAC units:
If refrigerant is required for an HVAC unit with multiple independent circuits/stages, keep in mind that each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance, so refrigerant adds on each circuit must be logged individually.
?	Example: if tech is working on PACU2, an HVAC unit with 4 separate circuits/stages, and wants to add gas to circuit 1 (PACU2a) and circuit 3 (PACU2c), tech or recordkeeper must enter a separate call log for PACU2a and PACU2c with the amount of refrigerant added.

Call logs are required to be entered in MyFacility within 72 hours of the refrigerant add. Failing to create a call log to record the refrigerant add within 72 hours is the equivalent of not getting approval to add the refrigerant. H-E-B will not pay for any refrigerant add that is not documented within the 72 hour window.

This requirement applies to ANY store/facility, any refrigerant type, including CO2, and any type of leak repair, including warranty work or any other special project.

Checked in with store leadership and located Cooler 3. Inspected the four hanging evaporators from the floor for any signs of smoke, burnt electrical components, or unusual odors. Found nothing out of the ordinary. All evaporator fan motors were running.

6/6/2026 - GJ
Clocked in: 14:15
Checked in: Julian (Manager)
Clocked out: 3:45
Checked out: GM Ray

Arrived on site for repairing Cooler 3 first evaporator and looking at Cooler 1 (Evap C) leaking water.

Checked in with store leadership and unloaded tools and equipment from the truck. Located the cooler and had product removed from underneath the evaporator. Was notified the store team could not provide a lift to access the evaporator at that time. Checked the facility for a scissor lift and found none available.

Gained access to the area underneath the evaporator and cleared the drain line with nitrogen. Filled a bucket with water, set up a submersible pump, and ran extension cords and hoses to begin deicing the evaporator. Due to the thickness of the ice, multiple trips were required to refill the bucket. Airflow has been restored, further ice accumulation has been prevented, and the drain is now flowing properly.

Part 2/2

Then began working on Evaporator C in Cooler 1. Found excessive water spraying from the evaporator. Gained access underneath the evaporator and inspected the drain system. Found the drain line clear; however, water was not flowing into the drain pan properly. Checked the drain pan level and found it was not pitched correctly toward the drain. Adjusted the drain pan assembly to restore proper pitch, but water still would not flow toward the drain.

Observed the water being affected by the airflow from the fans. Checked airflow through the evaporator and found very little air moving through the coil, with airflow instead blowing into the drain pan area.

At this time the store team was able to assist with setting up a lift. Checked airflow directly in front of the fans and found air pushing out the sides instead of straight ahead. De-energized the fans and inspected blade depth and orientation. The only issue found was a plastic bag tangled in one of the fan blades, which was removed.

Filled a bucket and raised it up with the lift to reduce the pressure drop from the height. Applied food-safe coil cleaner and sprayed the coil from behind. Retested airflow and found the water  was still being affected and poor airflow.

Retrieved a more powerful submersible pump because of the thickness of the coil.  Attempted to flush the coil from both the front and rear to completely clear any debris. Found no improvement in airflow. This indicates the coil is deeply impacted with debris, restricting proper airflow and drainage, and will require cleaning with an electric power washer while using a lift.

Notified GM Ray of the findings. He advised shutting off Evaporator C in Cooler 1 until repairs can be completed to prevent further water from spraying onto product.

Cleaned up work area and notified store leadership.
No injuries were reported on this job.

2 - Coil cleaner food safe, can be locally sourced
1 - Electric power washer (equipment needed)
1 - Scissor lift
 Hours required to complete work - 6
 Scope of work: 1 technician will need to unload equipment, use a lift, wash out the evaporator with coil cleaner and electric power washer. Then verify proper drainage, make any adjustments as needed.

10.	In Progress/Incomplete or In Progress/Awaiting Quote if we cannot repair same day.

I removed the bottom trays, placed the system into defrost mode, and verified defrost operation. During testing, I observed that the return air defrost heater was only drawing 5 amps. I thoroughly cleaned the strainer and verified proper condensate drainage and operation.

I added a small amount of gas and found the cap tube had broke on the fan cycling control. I removed fan cycling control and pulled a vacuum. I turned the unit back on and ran for a bit  but it was tripping the high pressure safety because of a bad fan motor. I got the coil wet with water and ran until box temp was down to 15 degrees. I ran to United and picked up the parts and return. I install and tested. The system is now running. I arrived at the store and checked with the manager. I went directly to the self-contained unit. The temperature was high. I asked them to remove the merchandise. I removed the covers and found the coil completely blocked by ice. I turned off the case, plugged the drain, and poured hot water onto the coil with my cordless pump. I moved the condensing unit outside, removed the control block, reprogrammed the Dixell control, adjusted the set point, defrost time, and defrost intervals, calibrated the temperature probe with the actual room temperature, and the self-contained unit was set to the set point. A note on HVAC units:
If refrigerant is required for an HVAC unit with multiple independent circuits/stages, keep in mind that each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance, so refrigerant adds on each circuit must be logged individually.

Arrived on site. Checked in with Denise Kirby. Upon arrival, I made my way to dairy multideck end cap. I found temp at 60 degrees. I checked if coils were frozen. They weren’t. I checked evap fans and they were all running. I made my way on top of case and looked at controller. I was inspecting controller wiring when I heard EEVs open and case drop into temperature. I didn’t reboot controller or touched anything. I then called EMS. They said it had to be a parameter in the controller. I went through all parameters. I compared transducer pressure with my gauge. Transducer is accurate. I compared discharge and return sensors with my thermometer. They are accurate. I then noticed case went into defrost. With gauges connected I monitored transducer pressure. After defrost my suction pressure rose to 102psi and then dropped to 55psi. I adjusted minimum EEV opening from 0 to 20 percent. I also adjusted max operating pressure parameter from 75 to 150. These adjustments will help with EEV shutdowns. EEVs won’t shut down anymore since MOP parameter has more range to allow higher pressure. I then made my way to microthermo graph. I found that the case went into defrost and stayed in high temp for a long time. As of now case is working properly. EEVs won’t be locked if pressure rises higher than 75 PSI. I monitored case for a while and saw it go through multiple defrost cycles. Unit is working properly. Call is complete.

I was dispatched to target 2474 for a call back dispatch. When I arrived I checked in on fieldjetx and with management. After that I went to the case and found the case A03 T1 at 1.22 degrees and the rest of the cases were lower than setpoint because T1 was so high it was trying to average out the temp and pick up the slack with T2&3. I noticed the green sensor on the honeycomb filter that covers the air supply was hanging and touching the frame of the door. This is why the temp reading for a03 T1 was off. When I mounted the sensor correctly it started displaying its true temp. The other cases that were too low in temp started to rise closer to setpoint and started averaging out to -8 with every case being within one degree it tells me that the cases are balanced. I watched the EPR dial back accordingly with the new temp reading. After that discovery I decided to mount all of the cases air temp sensors for A03 circuit behind the honeycomb. My reason being that I believe a worker or customer caught their hand in the wire and that’s why the wire became lose and come out of its zip tie that had it mounted to the honeycomb. So moving the sensor behind the honeycomb should solve that issue. I also discovered a fan unplugged on T2 so I plugged it back in and it worked. After the case got to temp I decided to run it through a defrost. When coming out of the defrost I noticed it was taking T1 some extra time to cut its fans back on. The other two case (t2&3) already had their fans back on. I dug a little further and found that the sensor that controls the fans based off coil temp had come loose. The sensor is just screwed to the fan housing and it either stripped and came loose or was never mounted. ——Notes continue on the next office notes box——

Either way I used some self tapping screws and remounted the coil temp sensor so that the fans would come on sooner and the T1 case won’t get behind. Without moving the sensor the case came down to temp and didn’t alarm but I want to be sure we fixed the issue so I went ahead and remounted the sensor to the fan housing. After remounting the sensor I put the system through another defrost to see if the fans would terminate and start up better and they did a little better. The sensor is mounted for the fans is mounted to the fan housing now and so are the others. The fans shut off within 10 min after starting defrost and they came back on within 10 minutes after ending the defrost. The case temps pulled down below zero (once the fans came back online after defrost) within 30 minutes. It went from 37 to 0 in less than 30 minutes. This case seems to be doing good now and it’s coming in and out of defrost as it should and it’s making target temp or (0) within 30 minutes of defrost termination, which should solve the case coming out of defrost and pulling down too slow. This is also not connected to the call back because it’s a totally different case. Yes it’s on the same circuit but the two calls are unrelated other than that fact.

Began preparations to pull a new sensor wire to the controller. Initiated a defrost and removed shelves to expose the back wall below the case controller. Began pulling the new sensor wire through the case using the old sensor wire, however the old wire disconnected during the process.

Reassembled all back walls, shelving, and bottom panels, and allowed the case to pull down to temperature.

Gained roof access to inspect the liquid line sight glass. Found the sight glass flashing. Checked temperature differential across the liquid line filter drier and found no measurable difference. Torched the receiver and found approximately 45% liquid level. Flashing sight glass condition should be further investigated.

Gauged up and verified operation of the remaining sensors, including the pressure transducer, discharge air sensor, and suction line sensor. Initially found the suction line sensor reading inaccurately. Repositioned and properly insulated the sensor, then verified the reading was accurate.

Costco #671 – POS Freezer Water Leak / Ice Accumulation
This call was for a water leak and ice accumulation within the POS freezer. We arrived on site, checked in with warehouse management, and were advised that the warehouse would be closing at 23:00. We then proceeded to size up the reported issue.
Inspection of the POS freezer revealed surface frost accumulation on the evaporator coils. The frost buildup appears to be the result of excessive warm air infiltration due to missing strip curtains at the roll-open door entrance. Additionally, the source of the water leak was traced to a condensate drain line that has been kinked and damaged from an apparent forklift strike, restricting proper drainage.
Repairs to the drain line will require a follow-up overnight visit. Corrective action will include removal of the existing damaged drain piping, temporary removal of the drain line heater, installation of new drain piping, reinstallation of the drain line heater, and replacement of any required insulation.
At this time, the evaporator frost accumulation is expected to be resolved through a standard hot gas defrost cycle once proper drainage has been restored. No permanent repairs were completed during this visit due to the scope of work required and operational constraints.
Findings: Damaged/kinked condensate drain line caused by forklift impact and missing strip curtains contributing to frost accumulation.
Status: Incomplete – Follow-up overnight repair required to replace drain piping and restore proper condensate drainage.

I arrived at the store and checked with the manager. I went directly to rack 4 and found all four cases of circuit 44 in alarm, but many of the circuits were far from their set point. I explored the possibility of a low refrigerant level, but after looking at several photos of the rack, photos I took at different times, I realized that the rack's suction pressure set point was constantly fluctuating. At that moment, it was above 52 psi and should have been 43 psi. I turned an override ON on two of the compressors. The suction pressure approached the set point, and all the circuits reached their set point, including the four cases of circuit 44, which was the reason for the problem. During the call, I accessed the suction group settings and saw that although the suction set point was 43 psi and the deadband was 2 psi, it also had a "float" system enabled where the suction set point fluctuated between 50 and 43 psi. I disabled this configuration and left the rack working with a suction set point of 43 psi and a deadband of 2 psi. After an hour of operation, the rack is at its set point, and all circuits, including the four 44-inch cases, are at their set point.

Problem:water leaking inside the unit

Resolution: Upon arrival, checked in with the store manager and proceeded to the bakery department to inspect the pizza self-contained unit. Upon inspection, found standing water inside the case. Removed panels and inspected the evaporator section. Found the evaporator drain pan full of water, causing water to overflow into the case.

Further investigation revealed the condensate drain line was restricted and not draining into the condensate pan. The condensate pan was dry, indicating the drain had likely been clogged for an extended period. Due to drain line location, removed the condenser fan assembly to gain access. Used a vacuum and drain adapter to clear sludge and debris from the drain line.

After clearing the restriction, poured water into the drain pan to verify proper drainage. Drain line operated normally and water flowed freely to the condensate pan. Monitored unit operation and confirmed no further water was entering the case. Reinstalled condenser fan assembly, secured all panels, and informed the bakery manager of findings and repairs. Unit operating normally at this time. No further issues found. Call complete.

Failing to create a call log to record the refrigerant add within 72 hours is the equivalent of not getting approval to add the refrigerant. This requirement applies to ANY store/facility, any refrigerant type, including CO2, and any type of leak repair, including warranty work or any other special project.

CUSTOMER :Px421
WORK ODER#4002055819
CHECK IN:09:45am
3RD PARTY CHECK IN: YES
EQUIPMENT : Deli blast chiller 
REFRIGERANT :404A
LIQUID LEVEL:flashing liquid sight glass
PROBLEM  : Chill blaster gets stuck in "defrost" (dEF).
WORK DESCRIPTION: After I checked in with the deli manager, I turned on the blast chiller, screen was displaying (DEF) DEFROST.I checked the Emerson controller it wasn’t calling for the compressor to turn on.I troubleshot the unit I found out 
the control board isn't receiving the proper signal that the evaporator coil is clear of ice. This prevents the unit from transitioning into refrigeration/chill mode.I checked the defrost probe I found out it was crushed between the evaporator coil and the front cover (pictures added).I repaired the defrost probe I put it into ice water reading was 32*(picture added).The  4th food probe was reading 51* into ice water.
I checked unit suction transducer Emerson controller reading was the same with my digital gauges.I turned off unit breaker and turned it back on, now unit is on refrigeration mode and all components were running, liquid sight glass was flashing suction pressure was 29psi =  -3* saturated temp(404A) while discharge pressure was 210psi.I leak checked and found a leak at the suction Schrader valve, I replaced it to stop the leak and I added 2lbs of 404A.I uninstalled the bad food probe, I monitored the operation of the unit, all 3 food probes temperature down to 36* and compressor turned off when food probes below 40*.We didn’t have the food probes at the shop, I contacted FSS Jp he gave me approval to order 4 new food probes.
CHECKED OUT:02:00
 CALL STATUS: Waiting for parts.
No injuries were reported on this job.

As of July 10, 2023, technicians no longer have to call (or text) the H-E-B refrigerant hotline to get approval to add refrigerant. 

Instead, technicians and/or vendor recordkeepers MUST create a “call log” in MyFacility within 72 hours of the refrigerant add, documenting: 
•	The appliance serviced.
•	The refrigerant type added.
•	Total amount of refrigerant recovered (if any)
•	Total amount of refrigerant added (including adding back recovered refrigerant)
•	Date refrigerant was added. 
•	Leak location(s) 

There will be an additional optional free text space for other notes.  

**PLEASE copy and paste the following link to access the HEB COMPRESSOR REPLACEMENT FORM:

https://url.us.m.mimecastprotect.com/s/OVkRCQWRVRFxmxD1SxfnTGgCW1?domain=app.smartsheet.com

Technicians and/or vendor record keepers MUST record refrigerant adds on the following appliance types:
•	Any refrigeration appliance except for self-contains (e.g., bottle coolers on the store floor), regardless of charge size.
•	Any HVAC appliance, regardless of charge size
A note on HVAC units:
If refrigerant is required for an HVAC unit with multiple independent circuits/stages, keep in mind that each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance, so refrigerant adds on each circuit must be logged individually.
?	Example: if tech is working on PACU2, an HVAC unit with 4 separate circuits/stages, and wants to add gas to circuit 1 (PACU2a) and circuit 3 (PACU2c), tech or recordkeeper must enter a separate call log for PACU2a and PACU2c with the amount of refrigerant added.

Call logs are required to be entered in MyFacility within 72 hours of the refrigerant add. Failing to create a call log to record the refrigerant add within 72 hours is the equivalent of not getting approval to add the refrigerant. H-E-B will not pay for any refrigerant add that is not documented within the 72 hour window.

This requirement applies to ANY store/facility, any refrigerant type, including CO2, and any type of leak repair, including warranty work or any other special project.
